title: 制御工学Ⅰ
subtitle: Control Engineering I
teachers:
MURAO Toshiyuki
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal:
(1) Learn to analyze transient response to a step input.
(2) Learn frequency response analysis by using vector locus and Bode plots.
(3) Acquire the capability to determine the stability of a system using the Hurwitz stability criterion.
advice:
This is a basic course in control engineering. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1. Transient response analysis using Laplace transforms.
2. Frequency response analysis using vector locus and Bode plots.
3. Determining stability of a system by Hurwitz stability criterion.

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
requiredKnowledge:
Completion of Introduction to Control Engineering.
Basic knowledge of differential calculus.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Obtain step response for second-order and higher-order systems
(2) Describe the vector locus for second-order and higher-order systems
(3) Describe Bode plots for second-order and higher-order systems
(4) Determine the stability of second-order and higher-order systems using the Hurwitz stability criterion
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Obtain step response for a first-order system
(2) Describe the vector locus for first-order and/or second-order systems
(3) Describe Bode plots for first-order and/or second-order systems
(4) Determine the stability of a second-order system using the Hurwitz stability criterion

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This is a basic course in control engineering. We will mainly cover the following topics:
1. Transient response analysis using Laplace transforms.
2. Frequency response analysis using vector locus and Bode plots.
3. Determining stability of a system by Hurwitz stability criterion.

Students are expected to actively participate in class.
Students are expected to complete exercises independently.
Students are required to be aware of the instructor’s messages in the class and to check for messages/materials on the KIT Inside website before every class because the course schedule may change depending on the class progress.
